name: DNREC Delaware Environmental Release Notification System (DERNS): Recent Releases
operator: Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control
access_detail: https://derns.dnrec.delaware.gov/Pub/RecentReleases.aspx (no login). Columns: Notification Issued (Y/N), Release ID, Location, Substance Released, Extremely Hazardous, Release Time, Facility, Status (e.g. Final), View (detail via postback). Search by facility, substance, city, zip. Sewage rows saved to raw/derns-recent-sewage-extract.json. Sign-up for email/fax/phone notices: Register on https://derns.dnrec.delaware.gov/ (account).

sample_record.Location: Approximately 100 yards East of #3 Pump Kent County Wastewater, 136 East Water St Dover, DE 19901

cadence: Within 1 business day of the report (statute). Newest rows dated the same day as the check.
history: Release ids to 17,756; paging to hundreds of pages (start year not checked).
legal_basis: 7 Del. C. 6028(a), 6014(b), 6002(20); DERNS policy (raw link Pub/DERNSPolicy.pdf)
status_reason: Statewide list of every environmental release reported under 7 Del. C. 6028, posted within one business day, including sewage releases of 10,000 gallons or more. Event precision (release time), facility, location text, substance, status, release id. HTML (ASP.NET postback paging, about 17,756 releases); a scraper is needed. Best statewide source for SSOs; CSOs in compliance with the permit are exempt.
notes: Two of the ten newest rows were wastewater (City of Dover sewage 2026-10-23; "WASTEWATER" on a Dover roadway 2026-10-18). Some locations are private residences (fuel-oil releases): never show non-sewage rows. Detail pages may include names; not fetched. A 2011 WHYY story found a 13.5-million-gallon partially treated Wilmington plant discharge missing from DERNS.

name: 7 Del. C. 6028 Report of discharge of pollutant (and 6014(b) central notification; 6002(20) environmental release)
status_reason: Release reporting to DNREC "as soon as the person has knowledge", web posting by DNREC no later than 1 business day after the report; DNREC notification to legislators and registered neighbours within 12 hours for sewage of 10,000 gallons or more. Permitted discharges exempt.
notes: Raw: raw/delcode-7-60-sc02.html. See profile citations for quotes.

name: City of Wilmington "What is a CSO, Anyway?" site
operator: City of Wilmington Department of Public Works
status_reason: Describes signs at every CSO and a real-time control system; no overflow status, map, list or sign-up.
notes: Quote: "Each location is marked by a sign notifying the public of the CSO."
